'''Jeremy Zico Kolter''' is a professor at [[Carnegie Mellon University]] and director of its machine learning department.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jeremy Zico Kolter |url=https://dl.acm.org/profile/81100095014 |access-date=2025-03-01 |website=ACM Digital Library}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite news |date=August 8, 2024 |title=OpenAI appoints veteran AI professor Zico Kolter to board |url=https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/openai-appoints-veteran-ai-professor-zico-kolter-board-2024-08-08/ |access-date=2025-02-22 |work=[[Reuters]]}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite news |last=McCullougn |first=L. E. |date=November 4, 2024 |title=CMU's Zico Kolter shapes new paths for AI safety and security |url=https://nextpittsburgh.com/business-tech-news/cmus-zico-kolter-shapes-new-paths-for-ai-safety-and-security/ |access-date=2025-02-22 |work=Next Pittsburgh}}</ref> He focuses primarily on [[AI safety]] research.<ref name=":0" /> He is a co-founder and senior advisor of Gray Swan AI, an AI safety and security company.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |last=Emerson |first=Sarah |date=November 8, 2024 |title=This hacker team is bulletproofing AI models for companies like OpenAI and Anthropic |url=https://www.forbes.com.au/news/innovation/this-hacker-team-is-bulletproofing-ai-models-for-companies-like-openai-and-anthropic/ |access-date=2025-02-22 |work=Forbes Australia}}</ref> In 2024, he was appointed to the board of directors for [[OpenAI]], and became chair of its safety and security committee.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> In 2025, he was named as a recipient of funding from [[Schmidt Sciences]] AI safety science program.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Heikkilä |first=Melissa |date=February 12, 2025 |title=Ex-Google chief warns west to focus on open-source AI in competition with China |url=https://www.ft.com/content/84cf0b2e-651d-4cb4-b426-ebc7afd634fa |access-date=2025-02-22 |work=[[Financial Times]]}}</ref>

Kolter earned his PhD in computer science at [[Stanford University]] and completed a postdoctoral fellowship at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Robinson-Johnson |first=Evan |date=August 8, 2024 |title=CMU director Zico Kolter joins OpenAI board focused on safety |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/business/tech-news/2024/08/08/openai-board-safety-cmu-director-zico-kolter/stories/202408080111 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240808222332/https://www.post-gazette.com/business/tech-news/2024/08/08/openai-board-safety-cmu-director-zico-kolter/stories/202408080111 |archive-date=2024-08-08 |access-date=2025-03-01 |work=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette}}</ref><ref name=":1" /> He joined the CMU faculty in 2012.<ref name=":1" /> His other corporate positions have included chief data scientist at [[C3.ai]] and chief expert at Bosch Center for AI.<ref name=":1" /> At CMU, he has worked on projects such as finding ways to automate assessment of large language model safety.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Metz |first=Rachel |date=August 8, 2024 |title=OpenAI Names Computer Scientist Zico Kolter as New Board Member |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-08-08/openai-names-computer-scientist-zico-kolter-as-new-board-member |access-date=2026-05-03 |work=Bloomberg.com}}</ref>
